Subject: PulseHealth DPA: initial asks (no‑train, subprocessors, evidence)

Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — PulseHealth is keen to move to a scoped pilot. Before procurement can sign off we need to align on a few DPA items so legal can clear the SOW:

- No‑training / no‑model‑improvement commitment on customer inputs (we need explicit language).
- Subprocessor inventory + contract flow (we need current list + process for adding/removing subprocessors).
- Evidence of data residency controls and KMS residency for onshore routing (EU/US split).
- Exportability/derivative IP rights — procurement prefers explicit non‑derivative commitments on model outputs.

I've attached our draft DPA (PulseHealth_DPA_v1.2.pdf) with inline comments. Procurement would like redlines back by EOD Wednesday (2026‑06‑02) if possible.

Can you confirm who from Redwood will provide: (1) operational description of the no‑training guarantee, (2) current subprocessor CSV, and (3) a short attestation / timeline for evidence delivery?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

— Alicia

Subject: Re: PulseHealth DPA: initial asks (no‑train, subprocessors, evidence)

Alicia / Marissa — thanks for pulling this together. Quick clarification and proposed language to make the contractual commitment concrete.

Operational clarification (short):
- "No‑training" means Redwood will not (a) incorporate customer provided prompts, files, or model outputs into any model weights used in our hosted public models, nor (b) use customer data to perform supervised or unsupervised model improvement of any of our public or shared models.
- We will maintain telemetry for service health and billing; any telemetry used for system performance is aggregated/hashed and retained for 30 days by default unless otherwise requested.

Suggested contract clause (for legal redline):
- "Provider will not, either directly or through a subprocessor, use Customer Content to train, fine‑tune, or update Provider's models or otherwise incorporate Customer Content into model weights, models, or training data used in Provider's externally‑available models. Provider may process Customer Content for the purpose of providing the Services and maintaining service health, subject to the data retention and pseudonymization controls described in Schedule A."

Notes / exceptions worth flagging:
- We need to be explicit about interactive session debugging and anonymized telemetry (already accounted for above).
- If PulseHealth needs absolute zero telemetry retention, we can discuss an isolated, dedicated deployment (Dedicated or Private) — that would be a procurement conversation with pricing implications.

I'll prepare a succinct ops description and the CSV of subprocessors for Kimberly to sign off and send by EOD Tue 6/1.

— David
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
